thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Struggle To Break Three-day Decline, But Bond Yields Remain In Focus

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Struggle To Break Three-day Decline, But Bond Yields Remain In Focus
text:
By Ryan Vlastelica
Tech stocks among the day's biggest outperformers
U.S. stocks were mixed in choppy trading, as investors continued to monitor bond yields and the implication that rising yields could have on equities.
Where are the major benchmarks trading?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 59 points, or 0.2%, to 26,428. The S&P 500 rose 1.67 points, or less than 0.1%, to 2,886.10. The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 0.4% to 7,768.94. All three initially traded in negative territory, and both the S&P and the Nasdaq are coming off three straight days of declines.
For a third straight session, the S&P 500 dipped below its 50-day moving average, a closely watched gauge of short-term momentum. However, it subsequently rebounded above it, suggesting it could be serving as a support level. The benchmark index hasn't closed below its average since July.
The day's gains were broad based, with eight of the 11 primary S&P 500 sectors in positive territory. Among the biggest gainers were tech shares, which rose 0.9%, and the consumer-discretionary sector, which rose 1%. Both have been among the biggest decliners in recent sessions. Among notable gainers on Tuesday, Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) rose 1.8% and Apple Inc. (AAPL) gained 1.3%. Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) rose 1.4%.
What's driving market action?
Recent trading has been driven by rising bond yields and interest rates, both of which could signal a new phase in postcrisis markets that have enjoyed a protracted period of ultralow yields.
Read:It's the surge in 'real yields' that could spell danger for stocks as bond markets swoon (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/its-the-surge-in-real-yields-that-could-spell-danger-for-stocks-as-bond-markets-swoon-2018-10-09)
Higher yields equate to steeper borrowing costs for corporations and investors alike, and have caused a reassessment of equity valuations, already deemed lofty by some measures. On top of that, richer rates of so-called risk-free bonds can compete against equities, which are perceived as comparatively riskier.
Climbing rates, however, have come against a solid backdrop for the domestic economy, with a number of economic indicators supporting the notion that the U.S. expansion continues apace.
Don't miss:Sure, yields are rising--but it's the bond market's velocity that threatens to throttle stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sure-yields-are-risingbut-its-the-bond-markets-velocity-that-threatens-to-throttle-stocks-2018-10-07)
On Tuesday, the yield on the U.S. 10-year Treasury note fell 2.4 basis points to 3.206%, though it continued to hover near its highest level since 2011. The bond market was closed on Monday for the Columbus Day holiday.
Bond yields are merely the latest in a series of major potential headwinds that investors are worried could end the market's lengthy uptrend. Traders also continue to watch for the latest developments on trade policy (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-trade-war-could-reduce-global-economy-by-08-in-2020-2018-10-08), as well as political uncertainty abroad, especially with respect to Italy's budget targets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-why-investors-remain-uneasy-about-italys-banks-and-the-doom-loop-2018-10-08).
Opinion:Stock market risks have risen in the past week, according to Elliott Wave (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-risks-have-risen-in-the-past-week-according-to-elliott-wave-2018-10-08)
On Monday, the International Monetary Fund cut its global growth forecast for this year and next (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/imf-downbeat-on-global-economic-outlook-2018-10-08) to 3.7%, which for both years is 0.2% below its prior forecast in July. This reflects weaker growth in advanced economies, rising trade tensions and higher oil prices.
In the latest economic data, the National Federation of Independent Business small-business optimism index fell 0.9 point in September, falling from a 45-year high (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/small-business-sentiment-retreats-from-45-year-high-nfib-says-2018-10-09) to a seasonally adjusted level of 108.8.
Tuesday will also see comments from multiple Federal Reserve speakers, including Robert Kaplan, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, who said that cyclical inflation pressures were building, but that inflation wasn't likely to spin out of control.
Patrick Harker, president of the Philadelphia Fed, is scheduled to speak later on Tuesday, as is John Williams, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, who will hold a news conference Tuesday evening.
What are market analysts saying?
Jeffrey Saut, chief investment strategist at Raymond James, said that the S&P 500's 50-day moving average was serving as a support level.
"We do not expect this zone to be violated. However, even a pullback to 2,817 would not 'dent' this secular bull market. This week there is a fairly strong negative energy blast due, but it should subside by week's end," he wrote in a Tuesday note.
What stocks are in focus?
Pinnacle Foods(PF) gave a third-quarter sales outlook that was below expectations, though it also forecast adjusted earnings that were above analyst forecasts. Shares rose 0.5%.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Google exposed the private data of hundreds of thousands of users (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-tried-to-cover-up-data-breach-now-will-shutter-its-little-used-social-network-2018-10-08) of the Google+ social network and then opted not to disclose the issue this past spring, in part because of fears that doing so would draw regulatory scrutiny and cause reputational damage. Separately, Bloomberg reported that Google has withdrawn from consideration (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-drops-bid-for-lucrative-pentagon-cloud-computing-contract-report-2018-10-08) for a massive Pentagon cloud-computing contract. Shares of Alphabet Inc.(GOOGL) (GOOGL), Google's parent company, rose 0.3%.
American Airlines Group Inc. (AAL) shares sank 3.3% after it raised its third-quarter outlook for total revenue per available seat mile (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/american-airlines-stock-climbs-after-unit-revenue-outlook-raised-2018-10-09).
D.R. Horton Inc. (DHI) reported fourth-quarter sales data that was below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dr-hortons-stock-falls-after-q4-sales-data-2018-10-09). The stock fell 0.3%.
Helen of Troy Corp. (HELE) fell 0.3% after it reported second-quarter results that beat expectations and raised its full-year outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/helen-of-troys-stock-rallies-after-big-profit-and-sales-beat-raised-outlook-2018-10-09).
Facebook Inc.(FB) on Monday announced the launch of Portal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-launches-home-video-chatand-promises-it-wont-spy-on-you-2018-10-08), a video-calling device meant to help users "connect with friends and family" with artificial intelligence-powered cameras, but some privacy advocates have questioned the timing of the tablet device's launch. Shares of Facebook rose 1.7%.
Trian Fund Management LP is evaluating a takeover bid for Papa John's International Inc. (PZZA), according to The Wall Street Journal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hedge-fund-trian-mulls-bid-to-buy-papa-johns-2018-10-08). The stock jumped 7.3%.
Perrigo Co. PLC (PRGO) late Monday named Murray Kessler as president and chief executive (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/perrigo-appoints-murray-kessler-as-ceo-2018-10-08). Shares fell 4%.
Affimed NV(AFMD) could be under pressure a day after the biotech drug developer put two clinical trials on hold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/affimed-shares-halted-as-cancer-drug-study-put-on-hold-after-death-2018-10-08) after one study participant died. The stock sank 22%.
Where are other markets trading?
Asian shares saw a mixed performance, with Japanese equities down (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-slips-but-chinese-stocks-bounce-back-after-mondays-plunge-2018-10-08). Major European indexes turned mostly higher.
Crude-oil prices rose, while gold was slightly higher on the day. The U.S. Dollar Index rose 0.1%.
